newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine power distributor plans real estate project.
newsitem.headline: Philippine power distributor plans real estate project.

text.p: Manila Electric Co (Meralco), the Philippines' biggest power distributor, said on Monday it plans to turn part of its 26.5 hectare headquarters complex into a mixed-use commercial and residential centre.
"By the turn of the century, half of this Meralco area will be converted into a residential and commercial centre," Meralco president Manuel Lopez said in an interview with Reuters.
Lopez said the Meralco office in Manila's Ortigas district, a growing financial and commercial centre, was bought for 60 pesos a hectare some 30 years ago.
Land in Ortigas now costs about 200,000 pesos a hectare, he said.
"We are now decentralising our operations and by the year 2000, we will only need half of this property," Lopez added.

Meralco entered the real estate business last year when it decided to convert an unused power plant in Makati, the capital's main business district, into a mixed-use residential and commercial centre.
The Rockwell property was once the site of a 200-megawatt oil-fired power plant run by Meralco, which now has a 51 percent stake in the 22 billion peso redevelopment project.
Lopez said Meralco expects its core business -- electricity distribution -- to post a significant hike in sales volume for the full year compared to 1995 levels.
"I think it will be pretty much that way, a 10 to 11 percent increase in sales volume, unless there is a strong last quarter and then it may go up to 12 percent," said Lopez.
He said the company's nine-month earnings were still being audited. He declined to give a precise figure but said it was around the 3.9 billion pesos forecast in a recent Reuter poll.
The company is expected to post a double-digit hike in sales volume in 1997 with a minimum of 10 percent growth, he added.
Lopez said Meralco and its customers expect to benefit from the proposed restructuring of the country's power sector.
Congress has started public hearings on a proposed omnibus bill that will restructure the energy sector, primarily by privatising the state-run National Power Corp.
Lopez said that although he supports the bill, in a position paper submitted to Congress, he opposed a provision which seeks to increase the franchise tax to 3.0 percent from 2.0 percent.
He said power rates will have to increase by 3.0 centavos per kilowatt-hour if the tax increase goes ahead.
Another concern is a provision creating a central procurement agency to buy power from independent power producers (IPPs).
"I believe utilities should be allowed to go into bilateral agreements with IPPs," Lopez added.
Meralco has entered into four power purchase agreements with IPPs that will supply the distributor with 2,355 MW of power up to the year 2004.
"Otherwise, we are endorsing this bill. It's good for customers since it will make power generation a more competitive business," Lopez added.
Energy Secretary Francisco Viray has expressed confidence that the bill will soon be passed and that the restructuring of the electricity sector will start before 1998.
